title: A navigation's refused download
assertion: `downloadHandler` answers a refusal to `Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate` with `Sec-Fetch-Dest: document` or none (and, without Fetch Metadata, to an `Accept` that ranks `text/html` above JSON and the wildcard) with 303 to the route's `returnTo` page, with no fragment: `refused=<status>` for each of the seven statuses, `fields` for invalid (parameter names only, each once, at most 8), `retry` for a rate limit in whole minutes from 1 to 1440, and the page's kept values, each validated with that page's schema; a relative Location, the cookies the request wrote and `private, no-store`; the signed-out statuses go where a page's refusal goes, with or without `returnTo`; the wrapper's own refusals (the codes, an ID that is not opaque) come back the same way; a link's closed `from` picks its page and any other value takes the route's own; the letter's bad codes, another payer's contract and a payer not the practice's each return to Coverage
noFileReason: The download routes are fake routes the test builds, and Coverage’s letter is refused on a synthetic practice the journey creates; no file.
